key_numbers.metric: Exact Match, StarCoder-15.5B Python, no-context vs retrieved-context

budget_tradeoff_detail: Retrieved cross-file context capped at 512 BPE tokens per example across BM25/UniXCoder/OpenAI-ada retrievers; adding retrieved context raises StarCoder-15.5B Python EM from 8.82% to 15.72% (oracle: 21.01%).
confound_note: Retriever/representation varied (BM25 lexical vs UniXCoder/ada dense embeddings) at matched top-5 snippets / 512-token budget in the retrieval-method comparison; the separate with-vs-without-context comparison additionally varies budget (0 vs 512 tokens).
stop_detail: Cross-file context assembled by retrieving top-5 similar code chunks via BM25 or embedding similarity and prepending them as comments to the in-file prompt, capped at 512 tokens (Section 3.3, experimental setup).
threats_to_datum: Retrieval baselines are generic IR/embedding methods not tailored to code structure, so reported gains may understate what structure-aware retrieval could achieve.

key_numbers.metric: Context retrieval acc@3, RepoBench-R Easy/Hard (RepoHyper+UniXcoder vs UniXcoder baseline)
End-to-end EM/CodeBLEU, RepoBench-P XF-F (RepoHyper-L2H+GPT-3.5 vs RepoCoder)

budget_tradeoff_detail: Final context tokens dynamically selected to maximize use of the LLM's context window; no fixed/matched budget reported across baselines.
confound_note: Representation (semantic graph + GraphSAGE re-ranking) and retrieval mechanism (graph expansion vs single-shot embedding search or RepoCoder's iterative retrieval) both vary vs. baselines, and token budget is not held constant.
stop_detail: A Repo-level Semantic Graph (function/class/script nodes with import/invoke/ownership/hierarchy edges) is searched via kNN-seeded BFS graph expansion, then re-ranked by a GraphSAGE link-prediction model before insertion into the prompt (Section 4.3).
threats_to_datum: No standardized token budget across compared methods, so accuracy gains may partly reflect using more context tokens rather than better selection.

key_numbers.metric: Code EM gain vs RepoCoder (API-level, avg)

budget_tradeoff_detail: Context window split evenly between retrieved snippets and completion context (max 10 snippets); GraphCoder needs one retrieval pass vs RepoCoder's 3 iterations, using fewer total tokens for comparable/better EM (Table 5).
confound_note: Both representation (CCG control/data-dependence graph vs RepoCoder's iterative regeneration-retrieval) and mechanism vary simultaneously; token counts differ between methods rather than being held constant.
stop_detail: Query and candidate statements are converted into a Code Context Graph (control-flow, data-dependence, control-dependence edges from AST-based static analysis); candidates are Jaccard-filtered then re-ranked by decay-weighted subgraph edit distance to the query graph (Section 4.3).
threats_to_datum: Efficiency/accuracy comparison is confounded by RepoCoder's need for multiple LLM calls (iterative retrieval) vs GraphCoder's single pass, so gains partly reflect a different compute budget, not just representation.

key_numbers.value: 18 languages, 100 val / 500 test samples per language, 5,993 test repos

budget_tradeoff_detail: Input length varied over {512,1024,2048,4096} tokens (max 4096); performance scales monotonically with more context, average prompt length ~1000 tokens.
confound_note: Baseline vs +Retrieval vs +Retrieval&Tuning varies both context content (adding cross-file Jaccard-retrieved snippets) and, in the tuning arm, model fine-tuning simultaneously; budget is also scaled as a separate independent-variable ablation.
stop_detail: Cross-file context is built by extracting L-line segments from same-repo files, ranking by Jaccard similarity to the in-file context, and concatenating top matches until a 4096-token cap (retrieval setting description).
threats_to_datum: Retrieval is simple Jaccard-similarity over raw line segments, not structure-aware, so results characterize a naive baseline; the +Retrieval&Tuning arm confounds retrieval with fine-tuning.

budget_tradeoff_detail: none systematically reported beyond stating retrieved snippets are truncated from the front if the prompt exceeds the LLM's context window, with generation capped at 500 tokens.
confound_note: Compares dual-graph agentic multi-hop retrieval (Requirement Graph + Structural-Semantic Code Graph traversal via ReAct) against Dense/Sparse single-shot retrieval baselines; representation and mechanism both vary, and token budgets used by each are not reported/matched.
stop_detail: A ReAct LLM agent alternates RGRetrieval (finds sub/similar requirements), DualGraphMapping (maps requirements to code nodes) and SSCGTraverse (multi-hop traversal of the structural-semantic code graph) tools to iteratively assemble cross-file context before code generation (ReAct tool pipeline section).
threats_to_datum: No matched token/context budget vs baselines, and the requirement-graph edges (LLM-generated, human-verified by only 2 PhD students) could introduce subjective bias into ground truth structure.

key_numbers.metric: task success without correction, multi-agent vs baseline
total tokens per task, multi-agent vs baseline

budget_tradeoff_detail: Multi-agent workflow uses ~100k tokens per task (3-5x the ~10-20k tokens of a single-prompt baseline) in exchange for higher single-shot success (80% vs 40% on 5 tasks).
confound_note: Compares the full multi-tool multi-agent pipeline (intent translation + literature RAG + document synthesis + Claude Code sub-agents) against an unspecified single-prompt baseline; tool count, retrieval, agent roles and token budget all vary simultaneously, on only 5 tasks with no statistical testing.
stop_detail: Code files are AST-chunked by function/class (tree-sitter) and embedded with a code-specialized embedding model for vector search (ChromaDB/Zilliz), combined with grep, then assembled turn-by-turn by orchestrated Claude Code sub-agents (Methodology section).
threats_to_datum: Evaluation is a single-codebase, 5-task case study with no statistical significance testing and an unspecified/uncontrolled baseline configuration, so success-rate and token-cost figures have very weak external validity.

key_numbers.metric: Exact match / Recall on small-medium repos (held-out queries)

key_numbers.value: tens of thousands of synthetic QA pairs from 6 data-generation strategies (S1-S6)

budget_tradeoff_detail: none reported at inference time -- the approach avoids inference-time context budget entirely by fine-tuning repository knowledge into model weights ('bakes repository knowledge into the LLM... eliminates the need for an external retrieval step').
confound_note: Ablates data-generation strategy (single-strategy vs merged S1-S6 covering file/module/AST/repo-summary granularities) at fixed model/training budget; not a context-window budget comparison since no retrieved text is placed in the LLM prompt at inference.
stop_detail: Six AST- and repo-summary-based strategies (per-file, repo-overview, mid-level AST structures, fine AST details, repo overview+summary, repo-batching) generate synthetic question-to-relevant-file-paths QA pairs used to fine-tune Qwen3-8B via QLoRA so the model directly outputs relevant file paths in one forward pass (Methodology, Dataset Generation Pipeline).
threats_to_datum: Ground-truth QA pairs are LLM-generated (via Qwen) rather than human-labeled, and evaluation requires per-repository fine-tuning on only 5 repos, so generalization to unseen repositories without repo-specific fine-tuning is untested.

key_numbers.metric: EM on CrossCodeEval Python (DeepSeekCoder-1B): AlignCoder vs RLCoder vs RepoCoder
EM improvement over RLCoder on CrossCodeEval
EM on RepoEval line-level (DeepSeekCoder-7B): AlignCoder vs RLCoder

budget_tradeoff_detail: none reported -- the paper does not report a fixed retrieved-snippet count (k) or token budget held constant across AlignCoder/RLCoder/RepoCoder comparisons.
confound_note: Both the retriever's query representation (query-enhancement via candidate completions) and its training objective (RL reward for perplexity-minimizing snippets) vary vs. baselines (RLCoder, RepoCoder), with no explicit control for retrieval budget/snippet count across methods.
stop_detail: A UniXcoder-based dense retriever, RL-trained to select the code snippet minimizing target-code perplexity, retrieves both Split-Aggregate base snippets and tree-sitter-derived dependency snippets using a query enhanced by candidate completions (Section III, Codebase Construction / retriever training).
threats_to_datum: No standardized retrieval budget (k/tokens) across compared systems, and graph-based competitors (GraphCoder, RepoHyper) are not directly compared in the reported tables, limiting comparability to embedding/RL-retrieval baselines only.

demote_reason: Full text confirms all evaluated benchmarks (BrowseComp-Plus, Natural Questions, LongBench-v2, Oolong-Real/Synthetic) are generic web/document/Wikipedia corpora with no software code content; the paper studies coding-agent scaffolding applied to non-code long-context text tasks (up to 3 trillion tokens), with no code repository instantiation or cross-file code structure addressed anywhere in the evaluation.

Full text shows the two evaluated benchmarks (OOLONG and CL-bench) use prose/document/tabular corpora (news, financial data, domain knowledge/rules), not software code repositories; 'code repositories' and 'OpenAI Codex' appear only as motivating framing/agent-architecture examples, and the context-map representation itself is generic text summarization (Context Roadmap, Context Understanding, Domain Constants) with no structural code representation, so there is no code instantiation of the proposed method.

venue: EUMAS 2026 (accepted, main track, per arXiv Comments field)

key_numbers.metric: semantic consistency improvement across folder levels (avg)

key_numbers.value: 6 repositories, depths 7-13, up to 293 files / 1,725 functions (turicreate)

budget_tradeoff_detail: Full child-folder summaries cannot be concatenated into a parent prompt due to context-window limits, so a keyword-extraction agent compresses child summaries into keywords before parent-level summarization; no explicit token counts are given for this budget.
confound_note: Compares the full three-agent bottom-up pipeline (summarization + keyword-extraction + QA agents) against HR-CS/CS-BF baselines; representation (hierarchical tree/AST vs flat), mechanism (multi-agent iterative refinement vs single-pass), and prompt content all vary simultaneously across 7 different backbone LLMs.
stop_detail: Starting from the deepest folder layer, a keyword-extraction agent distills each child-folder summary into keywords, which are combined with the parent's own summary and passed to a summarization agent, then iteratively refined by a QA agent, repeating layer-by-layer to the repo root (Section 4.1-4.2).
threats_to_datum: Only six repositories evaluated, evaluation partly relies on LLM-based semantic-similarity/keyword-coverage metrics rather than human judgment, and per-agent token/cost budgets are not reported, limiting reproducibility of the reported efficiency claims.

key_numbers.metric: Budgeted Context Yield @8k: RepoMap vs Qwen3-4B vs Qwen3-8B

key_numbers.value: 427 samples, 25 repositories, 392,000 files / 7.9M chunks, 308 base-commit snapshots

budget_tradeoff_detail: Budgeted Context Yield (BCY@B) computed at B=4k/8k/16k/32k tokens; best method reverses with budget (Qwen3-4B leads at 4k, Qwen3-8B leads at 8k on edit2ripple), and RepoMap (structural, vectorless) achieves the best single-method BCY@8k while trailing on raw Recall@20/MRR.
confound_note: This is the study's central comparison: representation/mechanism (lexical BM25, structural RepoMap, five embedding models, logged agentic Codex-CLI context) is varied while token budget is explicitly held constant via the BCY@B metric -- the cleanest budget-matched ablation in this batch.
stop_detail: Retrieval methods are scored by Budgeted Context Yield: the fraction of relevant content achievable within a fixed token budget B (via a regex code tokenizer), compared across BM25, RepoMap (path/symbol/reference/repo-graph signals, vectorless), five embedding models, and logged coding-agent (Codex CLI) context (Budgeted Context Yield metric section).
threats_to_datum: Relevance labels derive from real coding-workflow signals rather than exhaustive human annotation, and the 'natural no-gold' / counterfactual subsets are small (50 and 32 samples), so selective-retrieval/calibration conclusions rest on limited samples.

key_numbers.metric: compression ratio vs quality retained (Paritok-4B, line-numbered input)

key_numbers.value: 96.0% (96.2% held-out) of emitted tokens present in input

budget_tradeoff_detail: Paritok-4B compresses trajectories to 25.7-27.8% of original size while retaining 86.5-89.3% of uncompressed single-shot SWE-bench Lite solve quality, compressing 2.0-2.4x harder than GPT-5/GPT-4.1-mini compressors; self-hosted compressor breaks even vs. sending uncompressed context when hosting cost is below $2.23/million tokens.
confound_note: Compares Paritok-4B against GPT-5 and GPT-4.1-mini used as ad hoc compressors on the same trajectories/downstream agent (Claude Sonnet); compression ratios are NOT held constant across the three compressors (25.7% vs 50.2% vs 61.9%), so quality-retention differences are confounded with how aggressively each compressor happens to compress.
stop_detail: A 4B LoRA adapter over Qwen3-4B, conditioned on the agent's current task intent, extractively selects spans (replacing dropped content with closed-vocabulary structural markers like '[body: N lines]') from each trajectory segment (file reads, bash output, edits) before it re-enters the coding agent's context (Sections 3-4, per-segment distillation pipeline).
threats_to_datum: End-to-end solve-rate comparison is not statistically significant at n=300 (McNemar p=0.079), and compression ratios across compared compressors are not matched, so the quality-vs-compression tradeoff curve is only roughly estimated rather than precisely isolated.
